quick.summary: How to correct a teammate without making them defensive.
quick.takeaway: Point at the work, not the worker.

beats.line: I told my teammate their code was messy. They got angry. What went wrong?
You judged the person. Think of a trip to the doctor.
A doctor does not say you are broken. They say your throat is red.
So I need to point at the facts?
Exactly. Point at the work, not the worker.
Humans fall for the fundamental attribution error.
Can I just say judge the work?
Much better. Keep it about the code.
So I say, this file has three huge loops. Let us split them up.
Now you are solving a puzzle together.

quiz.question: What is the most effective way to give feedback on messy code?
options: This file has three huge loops. Let us split them.
You are not writing clean code.
Your work is getting a little sloppy.
I noticed you struggle with large files.
quiz.explanation: Focus entirely on the facts of the code, not the traits of the person.

quiz.question: Pointing out someone's personal flaws is helpful if they are true.
quiz.explanation: Even if true, judging the person makes them defensive. Judge the work instead.
